the results contradict the description: on a stream that has not been pushed back into it copies nothing. Called by the harness with a stream record poked as vsscanf sets it (text "abcdef", position and base at the text, count 6, size 6, flags 0x41, file byte 0xFF, no push-back) and (buffer, 1, 3) it returned 0, copied nothing and left the stream at end of input (count 0, flags 0x51) after one call of scan_stream_refill; the same through the scanner: sscanf_counted and sscanf with "abcdef" and "%3c", and "ab123" with "%2c%d", returned -1 and stored nothing. After scan_stream_ungetc('Q') on the record at text + 2 (count 4) it returned 3 with (buffer, 1, 3) and copied "cde", not the pushed-back 'Q', and with (buffer, 2, 3) it copied "cdef" and returned 2. The C calls scan_stream_refill at the top of every pass of its loop, before the first copy, and that routine zeroes the count before anything else
column5: (buffer, size, count, string stream): the fread of the scanner, for %c: until size x count bytes are copied it calls scan_stream_refill and stops when that fails, else copies with memcpy what the stream then holds (at most what is still wanted), and returns the whole items copied; as the game has it the refill comes before the first copy and discards what the stream holds, so on a plain string stream nothing is copied, the stream is left at end of input and 0 comes back (a %c conversion ends the scan as an input failure), and only when a character was pushed back into the stream's small buffer does it copy, from the saved position (the pushed-back character itself is dropped)
